newsitem.title: USA: Manitoba seen resuming power exports by Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba seen resuming power exports by Tuesday.

text.p: The Canadian province of Manitoba should be able to resume limited exports by Tuesday and halt temporary imports of electricity after storms destroyed two large tranmission lines last week, a Manitoba Hydro spokesman said.

The government-owned company expects to install temporary transmission from the northern portion of the province to the southern portion to replace two lines which normally move about 3,500 megawatts (MW) of power, spokesman Glenn Schneider said Monday.
"We hope to have something in place later today or early tomorrow morning," Schneider said.

The temporary transmission lines will be able to move about 75 percent of the 3,500 MW of transmission taken out by a storm last Thursday, he said. High winds toppled several transmission towers from hydroelectric facilities in the north.
"We should be able to stop imports and resume some limited exports," Schneider said.
Manitoba Hydro normally exports about 1,500 MW of power to Minnesota and North Dakota this time of year.
But when the northern transmission lines were knocked out, Manitoba Hydro was forced to cut exports and import power from the U.S.
Schneider said Manitoba imported 800 to 900 MW of electricity during peak hours over the weekend, and expects imports to remain near that level again Monday.
The reversal in exports pushed U.S. Midwest spot electricity prices higher late last week.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
